newsitem.title: USA: Australia sells one mln tonnes of wheat to India - U.S. sources.
newsitem.headline: Australia sells one mln tonnes of wheat to India - U.S. sources.

text.p: U.S. grain export sources said on Wednesday that India bought at least one million tonnes of Australian wheat in the past 24 hours.
"This is correct," one senior U.S. wheat export trader said. "They bought sometime during the past 24 hours, probably overnight.
"There was 250,000 tonnes Australian wheat for August shipment, 250,000 tonnes for November and 500,000 tonnes for December," the trader said.
Officials at the Australian embassy in Washington and the Australian Wheat Board in New York could not confirm the deal.
"I think we would have been told, and I cannot confirm it. They are sound asleep in Melbourne," a spokeswoman at the Australian Wheat Board said.
However, several traders said India had done the business.

"I am pretty confident it was done," a second U.S. wheat export trader said, quoting the details of the deal. He said one lot of 250,000 tonnes of Australian wheat was sold for August shipment at US$155.00 a tonne FOB, another 250,000 tonnes for November at $154.25 FOB, and another 500,000 tonnes at $154.25 FOB.
Another wheat trade source said he was "relatively sure" the sale was done with India buying Australian soft wheat at between US$155 and $160 a tonne FOB.
"It is Australian wheat, but I do not know the details as to the variety," the first wheat export trader said.

"If you look at the prices, I would say that these are the cheapest prices for a decent quality wheat," he said. The purchase details indicated India might buy more wheat soon for delivery before the monsoon season late this year, he said.
"Considering they have left shipment periods open in between, that is definitely the feeling of the market," the wheat exporter said.
